text.text:
Our experience at The Whaler was absolutely fantastic from beginning to end. The moment you walk in, the place has an energetic yet relaxed coastal vibe that perfectly matches the Santa Monica atmosphere. The ambiance is beautifully done- stylish interiors, great music, and an overall warm and lively setting that makes you instantly feel like you’re on a proper California beachside getaway.

We ordered the BBQ Chicken Pizza, Kale Salad, and the Spicy Tuna on Crispy Rice, and every single dish exceeded expectations. The BBQ Chicken Pizza was incredibly flavorful with the perfect balance of smoky barbecue sauce, juicy chicken, melted cheese, and a crisp, freshly baked crust. It had that perfect combination of comfort food and elevated restaurant quality.

The Kale Salad was fresh, vibrant, and surprisingly memorable. Often salads feel like an afterthought, but this one was thoughtfully prepared with excellent texture, freshness, and a light dressing that tied everything together beautifully. It complemented the richer dishes perfectly and added a refreshing balance to the meal.

The real standout, however, was the Spicy Tuna on Crispy Rice. Easily one of the best appetizers we’ve had in a long time. The crispy rice had the perfect crunch, while the spicy tuna was incredibly fresh, flavorful, and well-seasoned. Every bite had a great balance of texture, spice, and richness. You can tell real attention is paid to both presentation and flavor here.

Beyond the food, the service and overall experience made the visit even more enjoyable. The staff was welcoming, attentive, and created a very comfortable dining experience without ever feeling intrusive. The entire place carries a vibrant social energy while still allowing you to relax and enjoy the meal at your own pace.

Whether you’re visiting Santa Monica for the views, the beach, or simply looking for a great restaurant with amazing food and atmosphere, The Whaler is absolutely worth visiting. It’s the kind of place that gives you the complete experience- delicious food, beautiful ambiance, and that unforgettable California coastal charm. We’ll definitely be coming back again.

We had a disappointing experience at The Whaler and, unfortunately, it confirmed what many other reviewers have said about the 3% fee they add to the bill.

The fish tacos were the one bright spot—they were actually very good. Unfortunately, everything else fell short. The lobster mac and cheese lacked flavor and simply wasn’t tasty. The coleslaw was incredibly bland. The fish and chips arrived undercooked, with the fish still cold in the center, making it inedible. The clam chowder appeared to be leftover from the day before and was served separated, with the butter floating on top instead of being properly incorporated.

To top it off, we specifically asked for tap water, but our server initially tried to bring us bottled still water instead.  I would avoid this place.

Five stars for everything, but only 4 stars the back patio covered seating area. I can see this was supposed to be a temporary patio, perhaps during Covid, and they have tried to make it as cozy as possible. My only suggestion is to make the drywall look less like a construction zone. The only reason I am writing this is because I wanted to have photos taken of us by the waiter, but changed my mind due to the ugly drywall behind us.  I am not an interior designer, but maybe a wall covering? They did their best with plants and lights. The 5 star for this area is that one can bring their dogs,and it is much more quieter so one can have a conversation. The main restaurant is beautiful, cozy and inviting, but the noise level is too  loud and jarring at dinner. I don't know how the noise level is during lunch.

We all loved our food. I ordered 2 appetizers, chicken meatballs and crispy artichokes and this was filling for me! My friends ordered main courses for their dinner. My friend really enjoyed the Pasta Ragu and finished it completely! My other friend ordered the calamari and shrimp pasta and she really enjoyed it too. We all shared the tiramisu for dessert and loved it.

Oh! I forgot we started with a Aperol Spritz, which we really liked!

We will definitely return. I might try to venture to sit in the main restaurant next time! Ha!

text.text:
Spoiler alert: I rated this restaurant lower because of misleading Wagyu labeling. That said, Fia Steak is a very good steakhouse and worth visiting.

The service was the highlight of the experience. Every member of the staff was professional, attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely friendly. They made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived.

The restaurant has a very nice atmosphere, with an attractive bar overlooking the open kitchen and wood fire, creating a warm and enjoyable setting.

The Tuna Cigars were outstanding—easily one of the best dishes of the night. Creative, perfectly executed, and absolutely delicious.

The steak menu offers a good variety of cuts. Unfortunately, this is where my biggest criticism begins.

The menu labels some products simply as “Wagyu” when they are actually American Wagyu crossbreeds. For example, the Snake River Farms picanha should be described as American Wagyu crossbreed, not simply Wagyu. That distinction matters.

Would anyone accept ordering a bottle labeled Malbec only to discover it was a blend containing an unknown percentage of Malbec? Of course not. So why should we accept the same practice with Wagyu?

Restaurants need to start labeling Wagyu honestly and transparently. Customers deserve to know exactly what they are paying for.

I also tried the Australian Wagyu zabuton. It was less tender than I expected, leading me to believe it was probably a mid- to low-marbling Australian Wagyu crossbreed, although the menu doesn’t specify. That is exactly the problem with inaccurate labeling—you end up guessing what you’re actually eating.

Overall, Fia Steak offers a pleasant dining experience with excellent service, a nice atmosphere, and some very good dishes. My lower rating is not because it’s a bad restaurant, but because I believe misleading Wagyu labeling is something the industry should no longer accept.

I’ve been going to The Cheesecake Factory for years, even before I moved to the United States. It’s actually one of the places I always take friends and family when they come visit because I feel like it gives such a fun “American dining experience.” Their menu is huge, with so many options for every taste, which makes it perfect for groups.

This time, we went to celebrate my husband’s birthday, and as always, the food was delicious. We ordered from the SkinnyLicious menu because we wanted lighter options, and I honestly love that they offer meals that are less caloric without sacrificing flavor. Everything I’ve had there over the years has always been consistently tasty.

I also really love the atmosphere. Every location has the same signature look and feel, and I think the restaurants are beautifully decorated, warm colors, elegant details, and a very welcoming environment. It feels polished and comforting at the same time.

And of course, the cheesecakes are amazing. I’ve tried many flavors over the years, and not a single one disappointed me. They truly live up to the hype.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 for service is because of a small disappointment during this visit. Since it was my husband’s birthday, we thought he would receive a complimentary cheesecake slice, which had always been part of our past experiences there. Our waiter wasn’t very clear that this had changed, and in the end, we were charged for it. Later, I found out that now you need to be part of the Rewards program to receive the birthday cheesecake. If I had known, I definitely would have signed up beforehand to continue the tradition.

Even with that, we still had a great experience overall, and it continues to be one of my favorite classic American restaurants

text.text:
Santa Monica Nights, Cold Air, Warm Moments

We kicked off an early Saint Patrick’s Day this past weekend out in Santa Monica, and I’m not going to lie, it was one of those nights you just sit back and appreciate.
The place was packed. Energy everywhere. People out celebrating, music in the air, just a good vibe all around. It felt like the whole city showed up.
Now the only thing that tried to ruin it was that cold fog rolling in off the water. It hit hard. One minute you’re good, next minute you’re freezing. That ocean air doesn’t play around.

But even that couldn’t touch the night we were having.

My wife and I ended up at The Cheesecake Factory, and that’s where everything just settled in right. We were told it would be about a 40 minute wait for a table, but honestly, we didn’t even care. We grabbed seats at the bar instead.

Best decision we could have made.

We were already in celebration mode, so sitting at the bar just fit the moment. Drinks flowing, appetizers coming out, no rush, no pressure. Just us enjoying the night.

And the food hit. Exactly how it’s supposed to.

The Cheesecake Factory doesn’t miss when it comes to variety and consistency. The appetizers came out hot, flavorful, and right on time. No drop in quality, even with how packed it was. That says a lot.
What stood out even more was how welcoming everything felt. Even though we switched things up and stayed at the bar, there was no attitude, no disconnect. We were taken care of the whole time.
By the time our table was ready, we were already done eating. And you know what? That was perfectly fine. We didn’t need it. We already had the experience.

But let’s be real.

The best part of the night had nothing to do with the crowd, the drinks, or even the food.

It was being there with my wife.

Talking, laughing, just locked into each other with everything else going on around us. She makes everything better. Every place feels different when she’s there. More real. More complete.
That’s what I’ll remember.
Not the wait. Not the fog.
Just us.
And nights like that, you don’t take for granted.

Maria’s Soul Kitchen on the Santa Monica Pier was a really enjoyable stop. I was actually surprised that there was no wait when I arrived. The restaurant sits toward the end of the pier, so the location is hard to beat. The seating is open-air and the ocean is right there beside you, which makes for a relaxed place to sit and eat while watching the water.

The atmosphere stood out right away. There was live jazz music playing, people smiling, and the whole place had a laid-back energy that fit perfectly with the pier setting.

Service was very good. The hostess was friendly and welcoming when I walked in, and the waiters were attentive and easygoing throughout the meal.

I ordered the quesadilla and really enjoyed it. The guacamole tasted fresh, and the salsa verde had a really nice flavor to it. Everything came out quickly and the portions felt right for a casual meal on the pier.

Between the location, the live music, and the relaxed atmosphere by the ocean, this was a nice place to stop while walking the Santa Monica Pier. I’d definitely return. 5/5 stars.

My usual order is the Polish Taster Platter, which gives you a delicious sampling of potato pancakes, pierogies, kielbasa, and cucumber salad. I also love the mushroom gnocchi, and the gołąbki are my absolute favorite. For dessert, the naleśniki are incredible, especially the strawberry. On top of that, the place is wonderfully dog-friendly with a dog menu, which was great when I brought my Yorkie (who has now passed). I even introduced my Indian husband and his friends to Polish food here, and they fell in love with it too!

Summary: Not on my “Must Try” list of restaurants in Santa Monica for vegans

Food: I truly love Eastern European foods and flavors. I’m spoiled in this department with having access to many great restaurants on the east coast, not to mention my partner is Polish. I was excited to try the food here during a work trip as it came highly recommended. I only had one option on the menu, which was a beet salad. Needless to say I was really disappointed this was the only option on the menu that was plant based. On a separate visit I was able to try their vegan stuffed cabbage (didn’t take a pic) and found the flavor to be underwhelming. The salad tasted good, but wasn’t filling as a meal and isn’t interesting culinarily (been there, done that). The stuffed cabbage tomato sauce was borderline bland and the filling was the same. Plant based doesn’t have to be flavorless and boring.

Service: Any time I’ve been to this restaurant the service has been good. Servers are friendly, seem to know the menu, and are quick to make sure everyone is taken care of.  I prefer the outdoor patio in the back over the dining room. The interior to me feels very dated and a little musty.

Recommendation: I wouldn’t suggest for vegans to visit this spot when in Santa Monica. The options are very limited and need some fine tuning, in my opinion. I’d highly recommend the restaurant take the dedicated vegan items off the menu if they can’t improve the flavor of options like the stuffed cabbage.

Melissa is everything you hope for and more from a two Michelin star experience in Los Angeles. From the moment you walk into the intimate five table dining room, the evening feels special. The ambiance is understated and elegant, the service is warm and deeply knowledgeable without ever being overbearing, and the meal unfolds like a beautifully choreographed performance with every course more thoughtful and precise than the last.

The menu is a masterclass in balance, technique, and flavor. The Miyazaki wagyu first bite set the tone for the night, rich and perfectly marbled with layers of umami that lingered beautifully. The Croque Madame with truffle Gruyère fondue was indulgent yet refined, while the Caesar with smoked anchovy and parmesan was a clever and deeply flavorful reimagining of a classic. The golden tomato soup, paired with pistachio and strawberry sorbet and finished with Portuguese olive oil, was as vibrant and nuanced as summer in a bowl.

The progression of dishes shows a real depth of technical execution, from the delicate Santa Barbara spot prawn with umeboshi custard to the luxurious ossetra caviar course, every element was perfectly cooked, balanced, and plated with intention. The Wolfe Ranch “Dirty” quail was a standout, juicy and bold with apricot carrot curry and black olive caramel creating layers of unexpected harmony. The quail and lobster tortellini in carrot brodo was a study in finesse, and the lamb course and seasonal desserts struck the perfect chord between creativity and comfort.

What truly elevates the experience is the service. The waitstaff were impeccable, warm, intuitive, and eager to share the stories and techniques behind each dish, which added another layer of appreciation to an already remarkable meal.

Melissa is the kind of restaurant that makes an evening feel unforgettable. Highly recommended for a special occasion or simply to experience one of Los Angeles’ most accomplished kitchens at the very top of its game.

We came to Santa Monica Seafood for a birthday dinner, and it couldn't have been a better choice. Everything tasted incredibly fresh. The oysters and salmon were especially memorable—about as fresh as seafood gets.

We ended up ordering far more than we probably should have, but it gave us a chance to sample a good cross-section of the menu. We started with a half dozen oysters and the mussels before moving on to the branzino, cioppino, and Yukon potatoes. Everything was excellent, and the portions were generous enough that we brought more than half of our entrées home for another meal.

I'd only been to the seafood market once before, but this dinner reminded me that there's much more to this place than buying fresh fish. Since I work nearby, I've already decided to make Friday stops part of my routine so I can pick up fresh seafood for dinner on the way home.

Would we come back? Absolutely. Whether you're looking for an outstanding seafood meal or fresh fish to take home, Santa Monica Seafood is well worth the visit.

text.text:
So first of all let's thank The Misfit down the street for closing down their patio, since that's how we came to be at this gorgeous, high-quality outdoor restaurant for the first time. My partner's parents had offered to fund a nice gift dinner for us, and when our first plan fell through, we set to furiously searching for the perfect steak.

Fortunately, this great little spot absolutely made our night. It's a beautiful glass-walled garden with sofas and chairs and heaters: all the upsides of outdoor dining with none of the downsides.

We started by splitting a salad and a drink, and the staff separated them as a courtesy without being asked. The salad was quite decent in size and construction. The drink got us both pretty sozzled - very generous pour!

Then came the entrees and sides. My partner had the coffee-rubbed ribeye, and I had the salmon, and we shared each other pieces. Both were *amazing*.

Now, some background. I was raised vegetarian, & still eat less meat than average. I don't normally share my partner's taste for beef, but I'll try a bite now and again, and usually just become satisfied that I know my tastes well enough.

This is possibly the first & only time in my life that I've eaten a bite of steak and thought, "I could eat this whole thing. Gosh, wow, I *want* to eat this whole thing." It was juicy and flavorful and a delicate medium-rare texture. I now understand the appeal of steak in a way that I never did before today.

Fortunately, my salmon was also delicious, a generous portion, perfectly cooked, buttery-soft and hearty, with a mild flavor. And all the sides - broccolini, carrots, fingerling potatoes, black rice, an add-on of sautéed mushrooms - were also expertly crafted, and well portioned. So I didn't have to beg my partner for scraps of ribeye like the human golden retriever I am.

Now, I should also mention, she is a truly expert steak connoisseur as only a tiny anemic woman can be, having consumed hundreds of steak dinners over her lifetime. And *she* says it was among the top tier of steaks *she'd* ever had.

We finished off by sharing a perfectly pulled double espresso, to balance out the alcohol.

The staff were all very kind, communicative, and solicitous - I didn't catch everyone's name, but our server was Lily and she was fantastic.

Everyone was knowledgeable and responsive about our allergy concerns, so we had a great, celiac-safe, gluten-free dinner, with many options available. I would score this restaurant very highly on allergy friendliness. The atmosphere was good, and the warm, comfortable seating area was easily in the top tier of patios I've seen. We'll definitely be back.

Citrin started strong with comfortable seating and an appealing, well-curated menu. With a Michelin-starred restaurant, I naturally came in with certain expectations for precision, depth of flavor, and seamless service.

Overall, the menu composition was thoughtful and promising. However, several dishes lacked the level of flavor and refinement I anticipated. I was especially excited about the lobster pasta with additional truffles, which carried a significant premium. Unfortunately, the tomato sauce was overpowering, completely masking the aroma and taste of the truffle. Instead of a layered and balanced dish, it felt like a straightforward tomato pasta that could have been found at a neighborhood restaurant. Given the additional $70 for the upgrade and truffles, this was particularly disappointing.

Service also felt disjointed. There did not seem to be a dedicated server, and different individuals delivered each course. While everyone was polite, the experience lacked cohesion. Dessert arrived before the coffee that had been ordered, and the coffee never came, even after dessert was finished.

The highlight of the evening was the steak, which was well-prepared and genuinely enjoyable. Aside from that course, however, nothing stood out in a memorable way.

text.text: We had an outstanding dinner at Sierna. We also shared the sweet potato chips with charred onion mascarpone dip, a simple snack elevated by top-tier ingredients and clear attention to detail. The linguini vongole was garlicky, slightly spicy, and loaded with juicy clams, while a vegetarian pasta of zucchini, lemon, and parmesan was unexpectedly phenomenal—the kind of dish you dream of recreating at home but know you'll never quite match. We ended with the cinnamon budino, a luscious bread-and-butter pudding that left a lasting impression. A fantastic meal from start to finish.

two main things to make it a six star experience:

drop some mid dishes. some were really fun to eat; absolutely vivid; some I’d rather not eat. fix this then it would be amazing.

the service lacks natural hospitality that is common in (say) Singapore. waiters are very quiet for solo diners. no natural conversation in words or with facial expressions.

tip was solicited before card transaction.

Edit: the *total* experience lasted 1h 45m. The bill was brought out right after the last course. While I was still sipping my tea, there were emotionless peeking at my table, which was like a sign that I have overstayed my welcome.  In the middle of the dining experience, I thought it was so nice that I would come every month, but at the end I almost felt that I was kicked out like in a fast turnover restaurant.
